substitutes.name: whole_wheat_flour
substitutes.notes: Use 3/4 cup whole wheat + 1/4 cup all-purpose for best results. 100% whole wheat will be dense.
addOns: Add 2 tbsp extra liquid per cup

substitutes.name: oat_flour
substitutes.notes: Use 1 1/3 cups oat flour per 1 cup all-purpose. Make your own by blending rolled oats.

substitutes.name: almond_flour
substitutes.notes: Best combined with other flours. For 100% almond flour recipes, add extra egg or binding agent.
addOns: Add 1/4 tsp xanthan gum per cup

substitutes.name: coconut_flour
substitutes.notes: Use 1/4 cup coconut flour per 1 cup all-purpose AND add 1 extra egg per 1/4 cup coconut flour.
addOns: Add 1 extra egg per 1/4 cup coconut flour

substitutes.name: gluten_free_blend
substitutes.textureImpact: Similar to all-purpose when blend includes xanthan gum
substitutes.notes: Use 1:1 baking blends that include xanthan gum. Brands like Bob's Red Mill 1-to-1, King Arthur Measure for Measure.
addOns: Add 1/4 tsp xanthan gum if blend doesn't contain it

substitutes.name: rice_flour
substitutes.notes: Use 7/8 cup rice flour per 1 cup all-purpose. Best combined with other flours and a binder.
addOns: Add 1/2 tsp xanthan gum per cup

faqItems.question: What is the best gluten-free substitute for all-purpose flour?
faqItems.answer: A 1:1 gluten-free baking blend (like Bob's Red Mill or King Arthur Measure for Measure) is the easiest substitute. These blends contain xanthan gum for binding and work cup-for-cup in most recipes.

faqItems.question: Can I use almond flour instead of all-purpose flour?
faqItems.answer: Almond flour can replace all-purpose flour 1:1 in some recipes, but results will be denser and won't rise as well. It works best for cookies and brownies. Add extra egg for structure.

faqItems.question: How do I substitute coconut flour for all-purpose?
faqItems.answer: Use 1/4 cup coconut flour for every 1 cup all-purpose flour. Coconut flour is very absorbent, so add 1 extra egg and 1/4 cup extra liquid per 1/4 cup of coconut flour used.

faqItems.question: Can I make my own oat flour?
faqItems.answer: Yes, blend rolled oats in a blender or food processor until fine. Use 1 1/3 cups oat flour to replace 1 cup all-purpose flour. Note that oat flour may contain gluten from cross-contamination.

substitutes.name: ap_flour_leavening
substitutes.notes: Mix 1 cup all-purpose flour + 1.5 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp salt. This IS self-rising flour.

substitutes.name: cake_flour_leavening
substitutes.textureImpact: Lighter, more tender than all-purpose version
substitutes.notes: Mix 1 cup cake flour + 1.5 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp salt. Creates lighter texture.

faqItems.question: How do I make self-rising flour at home?
faqItems.answer: Mix 1 cup all-purpose flour + 1½ teaspoons baking powder + ¼ teaspoon salt. Whisk well to distribute evenly. This creates an exact substitute for self-rising flour.

faqItems.question: Can I use all-purpose flour instead of self-rising?
faqItems.answer: Yes, add 1½ teaspoons baking powder and ¼ teaspoon salt per cup of all-purpose flour. If your recipe already contains leavening, adjust accordingly.

faqItems.question: What's the difference between self-rising and all-purpose flour?
faqItems.answer: Self-rising flour contains baking powder and salt pre-mixed. It's convenient for quick breads and pancakes. All-purpose flour is plain flour without leavening agents.

substitutes.name: ap_cornstarch
substitutes.textureImpact: Very close to cake flour - light and tender
substitutes.notes: Remove 2 tbsp from 1 cup all-purpose flour, replace with 2 tbsp cornstarch. Sift twice.

substitutes.name: pastry_flour
substitutes.textureImpact: Slightly less tender than cake flour
substitutes.notes: Pastry flour has protein content between all-purpose and cake flour. Use 1:1.

faqItems.question: How do I make cake flour from all-purpose?
faqItems.answer: For each cup of cake flour needed: measure 1 cup all-purpose flour, remove 2 tablespoons, and replace with 2 tablespoons cornstarch. Sift together twice for best results.

faqItems.question: Why does cake flour make cakes lighter?
faqItems.answer: Cake flour has lower protein (7-8%) than all-purpose (10-12%), creating less gluten development. This results in a more tender, delicate crumb in cakes.

substitutes.name: ap_flour_bread
substitutes.textureImpact: Slightly less chewy, still good results
substitutes.notes: All-purpose works in most bread recipes. Result will be slightly less chewy. Add 1 tsp vital wheat gluten per cup for closer match.
addOns: Add 1 tsp vital wheat gluten per cup

substitutes.name: ap_gluten
substitutes.notes: Add 1 teaspoon vital wheat gluten per cup of all-purpose flour for bread flour equivalent.

faqItems.question: Can I use all-purpose flour for bread?
faqItems.answer: Yes, all-purpose flour works for most bread recipes. The bread will be slightly less chewy. For a closer match, add 1 teaspoon vital wheat gluten per cup of flour.

faqItems.question: What's the difference between bread flour and all-purpose?
faqItems.answer: Bread flour has higher protein (12-14%) than all-purpose (10-12%), creating more gluten for chewier, better-rising bread. The difference is noticeable but not critical for home baking.

substitutes.name: coconut_oil
substitutes.textureImpact: Similar to butter, slight coconut flavor
substitutes.notes: Use refined coconut oil for neutral flavor. Solid at room temp like butter. Works 1:1 in most baking.

substitutes.name: vegetable_oil
substitutes.notes: Use 3/4 cup oil per 1 cup butter. Oil creates moister cakes but doesn't cream. Add 1 tbsp for richness.

substitutes.name: vegan_butter
substitutes.notes: Use 1:1. Brands like Earth Balance, Miyoko's. Look for stick form for baking. Works exactly like butter.

substitutes.name: applesauce_butter
substitutes.notes: Use 1/2 cup applesauce per 1 cup butter. Reduces fat significantly. Best for cakes and muffins only.

substitutes.name: greek_yogurt_butter
substitutes.notes: Use 1/2 cup Greek yogurt per 1 cup butter. Adds protein and tenderness with less fat.
addOns: Add 1/4 tsp baking soda per 1/2 cup yogurt

substitutes.name: avocado_butter
substitutes.notes: Use ripe avocado mashed smooth. Works best in chocolate recipes where color isn't visible.

substitutes.name: margarine
substitutes.notes: Use stick margarine (not tub spread). Works 1:1 but cookies may spread more. Check labels for dairy.

faqItems.question: What is the best vegan substitute for butter in baking?
faqItems.answer: Vegan butter (like Earth Balance or Miyoko's) is the best 1:1 substitute as it behaves exactly like butter. For a whole-food option, coconut oil works well in cookies and brownies.

faqItems.question: Can I use oil instead of butter in cookies?
faqItems.answer: Oil is not recommended for cookies as they will spread too much and lose their shape. Cookies need solid fat for structure. Use coconut oil or vegan butter instead.

faqItems.question: How much oil equals 1 cup of butter?
faqItems.answer: Use 3/4 cup (12 tablespoons) of oil to replace 1 cup of butter. Oil creates moister results but doesn't work in recipes that require creaming butter with sugar.

faqItems.question: Can I substitute butter with applesauce?
faqItems.answer: Yes, use 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce per 1 cup butter. This works for cakes and muffins but not cookies or brownies. The result will be less rich but lower in fat.

faqItems.question: What's the best butter substitute for frosting?
faqItems.answer: Vegan butter is the only reliable substitute for frosting as it has the same consistency and behavior as dairy butter. Coconut oil and other alternatives won't produce proper frosting texture.
